A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLMOPT framework and experiments. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable: Appendices A–J in v1 and A–M in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLMOPT benchmark results, component ablations, larger-model experiments, and general-task evaluations in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds annotation-quality statistics, optimization-type analyses, and correction-mechanism experiments in Appendices K–M.

M1.justification: Section 3.3.2 revises the stated KTO loss specification by changing its reference point from KL(...) to beta times KL(...). The five-element formulation, multi-instruction SFT, alignment, and self-correction workflow remain intact. This establishes a localized change to the documented objective, without establishing changed implementation or retraining.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six optimization datasets and retain the ten general-task evaluations. Appendix L explicitly reanalyzes existing results by optimization type, and Appendix M uses the existing NL4Opt and IndustryOR datasets. Neither establishes additional dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: The principal comparator sets are retained. New Table 11 adds GPT-4o as an external corrector for LLMOPT and best-of-12 comparison variants for LLMOPT, GPT-4o, and reproduced ORLM. These expand the focused correction comparison without replacing the main baseline suite.

E3.justification: Appendix M adds a protocol using 12 repeated inferences with manual determination of whether any succeeds, alongside GPT-4o correction using the existing self-correction prompt. Existing training settings and main evaluation protocols remain unchanged. Table 10 newly reports smaller SA denominators for NLP4LP and ComplexOR, but its stated reanalysis does not establish changed splits.

E4.justification: v1 ablates the presence of self-correction; v2 additionally tests whether its benefits exceed repeated generation and correction by another model. Appendix L also adds accuracy analyses by optimization type across the six datasets. Together, these substantially expand the diagnostic evidence about correction effectiveness and uneven generalization.

E5.justification: Neither version reports across-seed variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new best-of-12 experiment changes inference selection, while Table 10 supplies success counts; neither introduces uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–3 and 7–9 retain their numerical results. v2 adds substantial diagnostic results: Table 10 reports type-specific accuracy, including 37.5% (3/8) on IndustryOR multi-objective problems. Table 11 reports IndustryOR accuracy of 46% with LLMOPT self-correction, 41% with GPT-4o correction, and 42% with best-of-12 selection. Appendix K also adds annotation-review pass rates.

T1.justification: The reference-point definition accompanying Equation 4 changes from KL(...) to beta times KL(...), a substantive scaling correction in the mathematical specification. The switch to explicit True/False conditions in Equations 4–5 is otherwise equivalent notation. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same framework contributions, optimization-generalization claim, six-dataset scope, and headline 11.08% average solving-accuracy improvement. The added appendix evidence supports existing core claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly identifies understanding database/file inputs for large-scale problems as unresolved. Appendix L attributes accuracy differences to formulation difficulty. Appendix M argues that correction matters beyond repetition and interprets ORLM's observed inability to perform correction as a severe generalization trade-off. These extend the interpretations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v1 briefly describes expert labeling; new Appendix K documents four processing stages, 12 annotators and their qualifications, two or three independent annotations per problem, separate review, adjudication, GPT-4o assistance, and feasibility filtering. This substantially improves documentation of training-label production, without establishing that the underlying process changed. Hardware, training hyperparameters, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Brown et al. (2012), Qian and Yu (2021), and Qian et al. (2025) to motivate security-game and reinforcement-learning applications. Appendix M additionally contrasts LLMOPT's broader capabilities with reproduced ORLM. The main related-work organization and learning-based versus prompt-based positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, expands the hallucination explanation, adds acknowledgments and cross-references to Appendices K–M, and updates publication and affiliation text. The main section order, argument, and most existing prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11, groups the retained Tables 7–9 on one page, and relocates some appendix figures and listings. It adopts ICLR headers and heading typography. Existing diagrams, plots, and formulation-example boxes retain their designs and content.

improvement.justification: Appendix K improves transparency about expert supervision, while Tables 10–11 provide useful evidence about type-dependent accuracy and correction versus repeated sampling. The KTO scaling correction also improves mathematical consistency. These are useful refinements to an already extensive evaluation. Important reporting gaps remain: Table 10 uses NLP4LP/ComplexOR denominators of 37/11 despite the retained full-set testing description of 65/19, and uncertainty estimates remain absent.
